chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: Make the G shape
exercises.purpose: Land the bright open G chord that starts a hundred country songs.

params.fingers: middle(2) on low-E 3rd fret, index(1) on A 2nd fret, ring(3) on high-e 3rd fret, rest open
params.strings_played: all six ring (low E, A, D, G, B, high e)

exercises.coaching: G is the bright, open chord at the heart of country. Middle finger on the low E, third fret; index on the A, second fret; ring on the high e, third fret; let the middle four strings ring open. That ring of open strings is the country shine.

exercises.name: One clean down-strum
exercises.purpose: Strum through all six strings without catching.

params.cue: listen for the open D and B strings ringing bright

exercises.coaching: Hold G and strum down across all six strings. Loose wrist. The open D and B strings give G its sparkle, so let them ring. If the low E buzzes, press your middle finger a touch closer to the fret. That full, bright G is the sound.

exercises.name: Your first boom-chick
exercises.purpose: Feel the country pulse under the chord.

params.feel: boom-chick — bass note on 1 and 3, strum on 2 and 4

exercises.coaching: Same G, now with the country pulse: pluck the low root on 1 and 3, strum the chord on 2 and 4. 'Bass - chick - bass - chick.' Set the metronome to 100 and let it sit. That boom-chick IS country rhythm. Just sit in it.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Today you learn the brightest chord in country — G. Three fingers, all six strings ringing, and you're already in the pocket.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: G: middle on low E third fret, index on A second, ring on high e third, middle four open. That ring is the shine.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Strum down all six. Loose wrist. Listen for the open D and B — that's the sparkle. Buzz? Closer to the fret.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: Boom-chick: bass on 1 and 3, strum on 2 and 4. Metronome at 100. That pulse is country.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: If you can hold G and play a boom-chick pulse, you've got the country heartbeat. That's the door to the whole style.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: G in your hands, boom-chick in your wrist. Most people think country is fancy — it starts with one chord. Lesson 2 of the pack adds C and you get your first real change.

lesson.title: Country Pack 1 — The G Chord (the bright open sound)
lesson.one_line_promise: One chord, and you're already playing country.
objectives: Form G (middle low E 3, index A 2, ring high e 3, rest open)
Strum it clean across all six strings
Feel the boom-chick pulse over a metronome
prerequisites: Em, easy C, G, D, Am (core open-chord set)
